raw_response:
Well, I've been doing this wheat-maize rotation for forty years now, so I've got a pretty good feel for what works on our ten mu. My husband and I are the only ones here — the kids are working in the city — and he takes some construction jobs in the slack season, so a lot of the day-to-day watching falls on me. At my age I don't have the back for everything I used to do, so I pay the machinery cooperative for planting and combining both crops. That's just how it is now in our village.

For the wheat going in this October, I'll stick with Jimai 22 — it's done well for me the last few years, good winter hardiness and the bread flour mills pay a little premium. I plant on the later side of the window, around October 10-15, because our soil warms slow and I don't want the seedlings too tall before winter. About 15 kg of seed per mu with the drill. For fertilizer I go with a 40 kg base of 15-15-15 compound before sowing, then topdress maybe 20 kg of urea at jointing in late March. That comes out to around 16-17 kg N per mu total, which is what I've settled on after trying a bit higher and a bit lower over the years — more didn't really add yield, less and I could see it in the color. I irrigate four times: winter water in December if it's dry, then green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Our well water isn't cheap with the electric meter, but skipping the grain-filling water will cost me more than the pumping bill. Expecting around 480 kg/mu if the weather is normal.

For the summer maize coming right after the wheat harvest in June, the turnaround is always tight — I have the cooperative no-till plant Zhengdan 958 directly into the wheat stubble within 2-3 days of combining, otherwise I lose too much soil moisture. About 2.5 kg of seed per mu. I side-dress 50 kg of compound with the planter and then about 15 kg urea at the big trumpet stage — roughly 14 kg N per mu, maize doesn't need quite as much as wheat in our rotation because of the carryover. Normally one irrigation at tasseling, two if July-August is dry. Should get around 520 kg/mu. I'll spray herbicide once post-emergence for weeds and watch for corn borer — if I see it I'll put out trichogramma cards, cheaper than spraying.

Pesticide on wheat is mostly the herbicide in spring and one fungicide spray at heading for scab if the weather turns wet at flowering — that one I don't skip, I lost half a crop to scab back in 2018 and learned my lesson.
